milestones.name: A GPU test in the sea, asset and cooker crates gets its device from one helper, and with no GPU it is skipped with a line anyone running the tests sees, or fails when a GPU is required
milestones.quality_bar: As dependable as wgpu's own `gpu_test` harness: one way to ask for a device, a skip that always says why, and no machine on which a missing GPU can pass for a run.

items.statement: `thrum-test-support` is registered in `.config/architecture.toml` with `test_role = "support"` and nothing has it as a normal or build dependency. The `test-crate-edges` rule refuses that edge, and for a package registered `"fixtures"` it refuses a build dependency and a normal dependency from any package but the registered proving ground.
items.check: sh -c 'python3 scripts/shape_rules.py check --rule test-crate-edges --zero . && python3 scripts/test_shape_rules.py'
items.ask: Do the rule's fixtures refuse a normal dependency on the support package, a normal dependency on a fixtures package from a package under `crates/`, and a build dependency on either, and pass a dev-dependency on both and a normal dependency on the fixtures package from the proving ground?

items.statement: A test asks for a GPU through one gate. With an adapter it runs. With none the gate writes `thrum-gpu-skip: <test>: <reason>` to standard error, where an ordinary `cargo test` run shows it, and the test returns; with `THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1` the test fails with that reason. `./dev check` sets the variable on macOS, so on this Mac a missing adapter can never pass for a run.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-test-support
items.ask: Read the gate and its tests. Do they run a child test process with the adapter forced absent, under the default harness with no `--nocapture` or `--show-output`, and find the skip line in its output and exit code 0, then a failing exit code with `THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1`? Does `./dev check` set the variable on macOS and leave it unset elsewhere? Does the gate reach wgpu only, with no type of `thrum-render`'s in what it hands to a unit test inside `thrum-render`?

items.statement: Every GPU test and bench in `thrum-sea`, `thrum-asset-gpu` and `thrum-cook` takes its device through the gate, by profile and restriction: `device-request` is at zero for those crates, and their tests pass with a GPU required. The sea's seven-storage-buffer device and its default-limits device are restrictions the helper is asked for, and what those tests assert is unchanged.
items.check: sh -c 'python3 scripts/shape_rules.py check --rule device-request --zero crates/thrum-sea crates/thrum-asset-gpu crates/thrum-cook && THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-sea -p thrum-asset-gpu -p thrum-cook'
items.ask: In `thrum-sea`'s `portable_limits_gpu` and its harness, does the device with seven storage buffers a stage, and the one on WebGPU's default limits, come from the helper, with each assertion as it was? Can a restriction raise a limit or add a feature?

items.statement: Every test that ran and passed in those crates before runs and passes now, and none is skipped on this Mac. The record holds the results of the same test command before and after, the later one run with `THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1`.
items.ask: Compare the two recorded runs' results, test by test, not their lists: does every test that reported `ok` before report `ok` after, under its name or a mapped one? Does the later run's output hold any `thrum-gpu-skip:` line? Does any GPU test in the three crates return early without asking the gate?

Nothing is run on Linux or Windows, so what is proved there is what a type-check and a read of the tests can show: linking, a lint-clean build and GPU tests on another backend are not claimed.

items.statement: `device-request` is at zero across `crates/` and `examples/`: outside the device recipe and the gate, nothing asks wgpu for an adapter or a device. The support package's stand-in is gone, and a test's device is the recipe's, by profile and restriction.

items.statement: Every library, binary, example, test and bench target in the workspace type-checks for Linux and for Windows from this Mac, with default features. One tracked command, `scripts/check_cross_target.sh`, checks `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, leaves no package or target out, and fails when either has an error. It links nothing and stands in for the C and C++ compilers. Warnings do not fail it.

milestones.name: The test kit's readback, device call and wait exist, and the check refuses a new hand-written readback or deadline loop in a test
milestones.quality_bar: As dependable as wgpu's own test harness: a test file holds what it tests, the jobs every GPU test shares are written once, and converting a test changes nothing it asserts.

items.statement: `thrum-test-support` offers each job of the kit, with a test of its own in the support package: a readback of a buffer, of a whole mip of a 2D, 3D or array texture or one layer of it, or of a byte range, with one bounded wait, on its own submission or appended to the caller's encoder; one call that asks the gate for a GPU, on Metal where asked, and opens the recipe's device by profile and restriction; one wait with a deadline; a scratch folder that removes itself; a PPM writer; and a counting allocator type that counts allocations and bytes on the calling thread. `thrum-render`'s unit tests have the same one call from the crate's own `test_device`, typed by the crate. No existing test is converted.
items.check: sh -c 'out=$(THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-test-support --all-features readback 2>&1) && echo "$out" | grep -qE "test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed"'
items.ask: Read the kit's tests: would each fail if its job misbehaved, such as a readback that returned the wrong mip or layer, a wait that outlived its deadline, or an allocator that missed a thread's allocations? Does the gate half of the one call deal only in wgpu types, with the recipe reached through the `render` feature or, inside `thrum-render`, through its own `test_device`? Was any existing test changed?

items.statement: `test-readback` (a buffer mapped for reading in a test file outside the kit) and `test-deadline` (a hand-written deadline assert in a test file) are rules of the shape check, each entered at the count of the commit this milestone lands on. A landing that adds one more fails `./dev check`, and the message names the kit's function to use and the Tests section of the engineering patterns, which describes the kit. The log gives each rule's count at landing.
items.check: sh -c 'python3 scripts/shape_rules.py check --rule test-readback && python3 scripts/shape_rules.py check --rule test-deadline && python3 scripts/test_shape_rules.py'
items.ask: Read the two rules' fixtures: does each refuse one more of its shape in a test file, and pass the kit's own readback and wait and the same code in a file that is not a test? In a scratch copy, add a `map_async` readback to a test file: does `./dev check-docs` fail and name the kit's function?

milestones.name: A GPU test draws to the test kit's one small target, and the engineering skill says in one short block how to write a test
milestones.quality_bar: As quick to act on as the testing notes in the contributor guide of a well-kept engine such as Bevy's or wgpu's: a builder about to write a test reads five lines, follows one link and has a shape to copy. The target is as dependable as wgpu's own test harness.

items.statement: The kit gives a GPU test its target, in a module named `target`: one call returns a colour target, with a depth target where the test asks for one, at the kit's one small size, in wgpu types alone, and the size is a constant that a test driving a host passes to it. The kit's own test draws to the target and reads it back through the kit's readback. Guard: the kit's test.
items.check: sh -c 'cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-test-support -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^target::.*: test$" && THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-test-support target::'
items.ask: Read the kit's test of the target: would it fail if the target were another size than the constant, or if the draw wrote nothing? Is anything the call takes or returns typed by an engine crate?

items.statement: In the engineering skill, one block on writing a test stands where the adopted-shapes table had its "Unit tests" and "GPU tests" rows. It says, each in a line that links to its entry in the patterns reference: prove a behaviour on the smallest world that shows it; test logic on the CPU and open a device only for what a GPU alone can show, at the test kit's small target; step simulated time, never wait on the clock; add to an existing test binary; a full-size or long run is a main-tier test and needs a plan's say. What the two rows said, the unit-test layout and the GPU gate, is one link from the block. The skill is no more than about forty words longer than its 1,657 of 21 November, and `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are as they were. Record: the check adds nothing to the tree.
items.check: sh -c 'f=.agents/skills/thrum-engineering/SKILL.md; ! grep -q "^| Unit tests |" $f && ! grep -q "^| GPU tests |" $f && test "$(wc -w < $f)" -le 1700 && for a in the-smallest-world logic-without-a-device simulated-time an-existing-test-binary a-main-tier-test; do grep -q "references/patterns.md#$a" $f || exit 1; done && ./dev check-docs'
items.ask: Does each of the five lines link to its own entry, and is the unit-test layout and the GPU gate, which the two rows gave, one link from the block? Did this milestone's commits change `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, or add test guidance to the skill outside the block?

items.statement: The Tests section of the patterns reference has an entry for each of the five habits, each under an anchor written out as `<a id="…">` so that its heading can change: `the-smallest-world`, `logic-without-a-device`, `simulated-time`, `an-existing-test-binary` and `a-main-tier-test`. Each says what to write, with a call or a command to copy where there is one, and what a builder does when the habit cannot hold: for a full-size or long run, that it needs a done-when item that says what only it can show, so a builder with none writes the proposal in the module's log for a planner. The entries state no limit of their own: they link to the test tiers of the project settings. Record: the check adds nothing to the tree.
items.check: sh -c 'for a in the-smallest-world logic-without-a-device simulated-time an-existing-test-binary a-main-tier-test; do grep -q "id=\"$a\"" .agents/skills/thrum-engineering/references/patterns.md || exit 1; done && ./dev check-docs'
items.ask: Take each entry beside the test tiers of `ORCHESTRATE.md`: does it say the same, and state no number the tiers do not? Does the entry on simulated time show how a test steps the engine's clock, and say what a wait on the device uses?

items.statement: The renderer's own record test, the sea, the asset crate, water and clouds hold their WGSL records to their Rust structs through the kit's one reflection check, in member offset, size and scalar kind. No crate keeps its own walk of a shader's bound structs or a second layout type, each `wgsl_records` test target keeps its name, and the checks that did more than reflect are as they were. A record that fails the stricter check is not changed here: its test keeps the comparison it made before, and the log names the record and the module that owns it.
